title: Forgetting await
why: Browser actions are asynchronous. Without `await`, the test will finish before the page even loads!

title: String vs Regex in Title Assertion
why: If the actual title is "Fast and reliable end-to-end testing for modern web apps | Playwright", the exact string check will fail. The regex `/Playwright/` checks if it *contains* the word.

title: Skipping Browser Installation
wrong: Running `npx playwright test` immediately after cloning a repo without installing browsers.
why: Playwright downloads its own custom browser binaries. Without them, it cannot launch the browsers.

title: Forgetting `--project`
why: If you don't specify a project, Playwright runs the test across all configured browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) simultaneously, which can be visually overwhelming when debugging in headed mode.

title: Stale Reports
wrong: Relying on an old `playwright-report` folder without re-running tests.
correct: The report updates automatically, but always verify the timestamp in the report header.
why:
**Mistake 2: Stale Reports**  
**Wrong:** Relying on an old `playwright-report` folder without re-running tests.  
**Correct:** The report updates automatically, but always verify the timestamp in the report header.

title: Hardcoding URLs in Tests
why: If the URL changes (e.g., testing against staging vs prod), you would have to update hundreds of tests manually.

title: Locators Inside the Spec File
why: Tests should read like business requirements, completely decoupled from the underlying DOM selectors.

title: Skipping Fixtures
wrong: Manually instantiating `const todoPage = new TodoPage(page);` in a `beforeEach` hook.
correct: Use `test.extend` to inject the POM directly into the test arguments.
why: Fixtures are the modern Playwright way. They support automatic cleanup, lazy loading, and parallel execution isolation natively.
